attempts.summary: Built a redundant transit topology between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), each serving a private network (node3, node4 respectively), so node3 and node4 keep reaching each other across either of the two independent transit links. Discovered the physical wiring via STP bridge-ID correlation (node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 = Transit A; node1 eth2<->node2 vtnet2 = Transit B; node1 eth3<->node3 enp8s0 = Private-A; node2 vtnet3<->node4 enp8s0 = Private-B). Configured VyOS with an ECMP static route (two next-hops, each pinned to its own interface to avoid FRR's recursive-via-default fallback when a link drops) and OPNsense with two monitored gateways (GW_T1/GW_T2) in a gateway group compiled into a pf 'route-to' rule for node4-initiated traffic, plus a real FreeBSD multipath kernel route (net.route.multipath=1, persisted via config.xml sysctl + an rc.syshook boot script) to correctly handle the reverse/asymmetric path for node3-initiated traffic. Validated failover live: started a continuous ping from node3 to node4, administratively disabled node1's eth1 (Transit A), watched OPNsense's dpinger mark GW_T1 down and the pf rule auto-recompile to the single surviving path, observed ~41 dropped pings during the ~45s convergence window, then confirmed the ping stream resumed and continued successfully — demonstrating continuity across the transition. Re-enabled eth1 and confirmed both gateways returned online and ECMP was restored on both routers. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured a pre-restart boot identity and health baseline for all four nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time (never overlapping), polled each until exec was available again, proved each node's boot identity changed, and verified post-restart that all addressing, routes, gateway health, and end-to-end node3<->node4 connectivity fully recovered (catching and permanently fixing a boot-time race on node2 where only one of the two multipath routes was reinstalled).
